correctness.rationale: An idempotent strict graph endomorphism retracts C_n onto its image, which if proper must be a path of k consecutive cycle vertices. The complement maps to a length n-k+1 nearest-neighbor walk between fixed path endpoints; n placements give e_{n,k}=n(A_k^{n-k+1})_{1,k}. For even n, the two extremal eigenmodes of path adjacency have combined amplitude 4 sin²(pi/(k+1))/(k+1), giving a saddle exponent a j + pi² n/(2j²) at j=(pi²/log2)^{1/3} n^{1/3}. A localized discrete Gaussian Laplace sum yields 16 sqrt(2 pi a s/3)*2^n*n^{1/6} exp(-(3/2)a s n^{1/3}) and centered n^{1/6} rank CLT. Independent exhaustive enumeration of ALL strict endomorphisms via closed +/-1 cycle walks for n=4,6,8,10,12,14,16 exactly matched every rank count and totals 9,25,73,221,685,2157,6881. Odd n gives only automorphism idempotent identity.
residual_risks: Infinite spectral tail control uses positivity and uniform j-window estimates; finite n checks do not certify it.

Although their cubic-root location and normal scale resemble published path and range-penalized-walk laws, neither exact cycle rank counts nor the sharp prefactor and rarity constant are implied by those other boundary conditions. value.rationale: Strict cycle graph endomorphisms form a natural finite transformation monoid. Their exact idempotent image-rank enumerator, sharp stretched-exponential total and explicit centered CLT give genuinely useful algebraic and probabilistic invariants (including rare-retraction counts and typical image geometry); unlike an arbitrary small computation, they solve all even n and provide a specific boundary-conditioned prefactor not supplied by the compared path or weak-cycle results.
